profile.campus: Centeris South Hill campus, Puyallup WA (86 acres, 2 buildings: SH1, SH2)
profile.reading:
This registry row, generically named Centeris and not tied to a specific South Hill campus building, carries company level detail for Centeris, the operator of an 86 acre private data center campus known as South Hill, near Puyallup, Washington, in the greater Seattle region roughly 35 miles south of downtown Seattle. Centeris is 100 percent owned by The Benaroya Company, a Pacific Northwest real estate firm with more than 60 years in the region, per Centeris' own about page. The South Hill campus comprises two buildings tracked separately elsewhere in this registry, a 56,000 square foot LEED Gold SH1 building and a 176,000 square foot SH2 powered shell, per a November 2, 2017 Data Center Frontier article on a 7 megawatt lease to tenant Colocation Northwest, operated by IsoFusion, an arrangement that resolves a naming ambiguity an earlier pass on this operator had flagged, since Colocation Northwest is a tenant within the Centeris campus rather than an unrelated, competing operator. A more recent October 22, 2025 Data Center Dynamics report describes the campus, naming it the South Hill Business and Technology Center at 1023 39th Avenue Southeast, Puyallup, Washington 98374, and states Centeris invested nearly 200 million dollars over the prior 18 months to expand the campus to 24 megawatts of critical load including liquid cooled racks for AI and cloud customers, with tenants including ScaleMatrix, which joined in March 2019 per regional economic development coverage, and Chunghwa Telecom Global, and a direct connection to the Westin Building Exchange, Seattle's major carrier hotel. An earlier Seattle Times feature describes the campus as the first transpacific data hub designed to store and connect data between Asia and the US West Coast, built in 2008 and remodeled in 2011 in partnership with network provider Wave, totaling 376,000 square feet across its two buildings with nine backup generators and natural air cooling.

This registry row's stored coordinates sit within about 30 meters of those recorded for the SH2 Build to Suit row elsewhere in this registry, far closer than the roughly 220 meter separation from the SH1 Colocation row's coordinates, and this row carries no address tags of its own beyond the shared campus address. That pattern is consistent with the working read already on file for this row, that it functions as a company or campus level map entry for Centeris rather than a distinct third structure, and it is treated here as a sibling of, rather than an addition to, the two named South Hill buildings tracked separately elsewhere in this registry. City of Puyallup planning records add a further local government data point for the shared campus. In February 2022, an application was filed with the city, case PLCPR20220026, covering an 86.67 acre parcel on 39th Avenue Southeast bounded on the east by Pierce College, a description matching the South Hill campus, describing current uses as office, warehouse, and data center, and proposing a rezone to Mixed Use Center with Urban Center zoning that would have allowed added residential and flexible uses. City records show the application was cancelled at the applicant's own request in May 2022, so the rezone never proceeded.

reading.body:
Centeris operates the South Hill campus, an 86-acre private data center facility near Puyallup, Washington, roughly 35 miles south of Seattle. The campus comprises two buildings, SH1 and SH2, with a combined 376,000 square feet of space. The operator published 24 megawatts of critical IT load capacity as of October 2025, following a near-$200 million expansion in the prior 18 months that added liquid-cooled racks for AI and cloud customers.

At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 24 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 600 racks. The campus serves multiple tenants including ScaleMatrix and Chunghwa Telecom Global, and maintains a direct connection to the Westin Building Exchange, Seattle's major carrier hotel. The facility was originally built in 2008 as a transpacific data hub for Asia-US West Coast connectivity and was remodeled in 2011 with nine backup generators and natural air cooling.

Centeris ranks third by published megawatt capacity in Washington State, behind only two other facilities. The state has 46 mapped data center facilities, but only three operators have published capacity figures for a statewide total of 60 megawatts, meaning this single campus represents 40 percent of all published capacity in the state.
